summary: Backend-only cross-tenant / portal isolation security test for PulseFitness.ai (commercial vs MOD vs master-admin). Ran 25 parametrized checks. 24/25 pass. All critical MOD data endpoints (dashboard, service-providers, quotes, equipment, staff) correctly reject commercial user with 403. All master-admin endpoints reject both commercial and normal MOD users with 401/403. Unauthenticated calls uniformly 401/403. MOD user cannot see foreign commercial data (Third Space / iso markers absent) on /api/equipment, /api/faults, /api/memberships, /api/dashboard. Cross-record fetches with non-owned IDs return 403/404. ONE finding: GET /api/mod/me returns 200 for a commercial (non-MOD) user, leaking that user's OWN org context (id=iso-demo-org, name=Iso Demo Fitness) through the MOD-portal surface. No other tenant's MOD data is disclosed, so this is NOT a cross-tenant data breach, but it is a portal-scoping / defence-in-depth gap — every other /api/mod/site/* endpoint calls _require_mod_site(user); /api/mod/me only calls get_current_user.

minor.issue: Commercial (non-MOD) authenticated user receives 200 with their own org context. Priority HIGH (portal-isolation defence-in-depth), NOT CRITICAL (no MOD-tenant data leaked). All other /api/mod/site/* endpoints correctly enforce MOD scope via _require_mod_site.

action_items: Add a MOD-scope guard to GET /api/mod/me in backend/routes/mod_portal.py (line 383). Replace `user: dict = Depends(get_current_user)` with a call to `_require_mod_site(user)` (or `_require_mod(user)`) so commercial / non-MOD accounts receive 403 instead of 200. This aligns /mod/me with every sibling MOD endpoint and closes a portal-scoping gap flagged by ISO1.
critical_code_review_comments: mod_portal.py:383 /mod/me lacks MOD account_type/org guard — inconsistency with all other /mod/site/* handlers that enforce _require_mod_site.

Login rate-limiter is aggressive (~4 attempts/min per email) and returned 429 during the first suite run — mitigated in tests by portal-aware caching and pacing. Not a bug, but flag for future test authors.

rca of the issue: Endpoint GET /api/mod/me (backend/routes/mod_portal.py line 383-401) declares only `user: dict = Depends(get_current_user)` and immediately calls `_org_of(user)` which returns the user's own organization regardless of account_type. Every other MOD site endpoint (e.g. /mod/site/dashboard line 404) instead calls `_require_mod_site(user)` which raises 403 for non-MOD accounts. Reproduction: (1) POST /api/auth/login {email:'owner@isodemo.com',password:'IsoDemo123!'} → token; (2) GET /api/mod/me with Bearer token → HTTP 200 with body {"org":{"id":"iso-demo-org","account_type":"full",...},"user":{...}}. Mitigation: change signature to depend on `_require_mod_site` (or an equivalent MOD-role guard) so non-MOD accounts get HTTP 403. Impact: LOW-MEDIUM — the endpoint only echoes the caller's own org, so no cross-tenant leak, but it violates the strict portal-boundary promise and gives a commercial account a working MOD-shaped response it should never receive.
